answer: Divergent Commitment Ledger: each agent periodically signs a chained state root, and peers reject any identity whose root replays another's history instead of diverging on fresh randomness. Clones cannot fork independently, so a jade cluster collapses to one lineage. Enforcement costs an attacker a unique unpredictable seed per identity plus a full commitment chain, priced as ongoing storage and signing work amortized across sable inactivity windows, making mass parallelism linear in real resources rather than nominal accounts; a lagoon of aliases yields no throughput gain.
